record.paper_title: Nine open problems on conjunctive and Boolean grammars
record.original_question: Are all languages generated by Boolean grammars contained in deterministic space DSPACE(n^(1-epsilon)) for some positive epsilon, thereby improving the known linear-space upper bound for recognizing Boolean grammar languages?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Boolean grammar is a quadruple G = (Σ, N, R, S), where Σ is a finite alphabet of terminal symbols, N is a finite set of nonterminal symbols, S ∈ N is a start symbol, and R is a finite set of rules of the form
   A → α₁ & … & α_m & ¬β₁ & … & ¬β_n,
with m ≥ 1, n ≥ 0, and each α_i, β_j ∈ (Σ ∪ N)*. The language L(G) ⊆ Σ* generated by G is defined as the unique (or, in general, the chosen well-founded) solution of the associated system of language equations
   A = ⋂_i α_i ∩ ⋂_j ¬β_j (for each A ∈ N),
and L(G) is the component corresponding to S. Conjunctive grammars are the special case with n = 0.

It is known that every language generated by a Boolean grammar is recognizable in deterministic space O(n), i.e., lies in DSPACE(n).

Question: Does there exist a constant ε > 0 such that every language generated by a Boolean grammar lies in DSPACE(n^{1−ε})? Equivalently, can the linear deterministic space upper bound for recognition of Boolean grammar languages be improved to a sublinear deterministic space bound?
artifact.status_search_result: The best known deterministic space upper bound for languages generated by Boolean grammars remains DSPACE(n) (linear space). No sublinear deterministic space algorithm has been reported in the literature, and the question of whether such an improvement is possible appears to remain open. Related work notes that conjunctive grammars can express P-complete languages, which suggests substantial obstacles to drastic improvements but does not resolve the sublinear-space question.

status_evidence.title: Boolean Grammars (Okhotin)
status_evidence.snippet: Family generated by Boolean grammars is contained in DTIME(n^{2.376}) ∩ DSPACE(n).
status_evidence.claim: The known upper bound is linear deterministic space; no sublinear bound is reported.

status_evidence.title: Conjunctive and Boolean grammars: The true general case of the context-free grammars
status_evidence.snippet: Survey covering complexity and open questions for conjunctive and Boolean grammars.
status_evidence.claim: Recent surveys continue to list the linear-space bound as the best known, indicating the sublinear-space question remains open.
